title: REPORT on amendments to Parliament’s Rules of Procedure on proxy voting during pregnancy and immediately after childbirth
section: Rule 193 a – title (new) | Rule 193 a – paragraph 1 (new) | Rule 193 a – paragraph 3 (new) | Rule 193 a – paragraph 4 (new) | Rule 193 a – paragraph 5 (new) | Rule 193 a – paragraph 6 (new) | Rule 193 a – paragraph 7 (new) | Rule 193 a – paragraph 8 (new)
part_text: Amendment Rule 193a Voting by proxy during pregnancy and immediately after childbirth / Amendment 1. By way of derogation from Rule 193, a Member who is pregnant or has given birth may have her vote cast in plenary by another Member acting as proxy, for a maximum period of three months before the estimated date of birth and for a maximum period of six months after the birth. / Amendment 3. The delegating Member shall designate a Member of her political group as her proxy, with that Member’s consent. Where the delegating Member concerned is a non-attached Member, that delegating Member shall designate another non-attached Member as her proxy, with that Member’s consent. The delegating Member shall inform the President of the proxy agreement. The delegation shall take effect from the beginning of the part-session following registration by the President or the later date specified by the delegating Member. The delegation shall apply to entire part-sessions. The delegation shall end on the date specified by the delegating Member and, in any case, six months after the date of birth, if either Member ceases to be a Member or if either Member joins or leaves a political group. The delegating Member may revoke the delegation or designate a new proxy, and the proxy may terminate the delegation. The revocation or termination shall take effect from the beginning of the part-session following its registration by the President. A new delegation shall, upon registration by the President, replace any previous delegation. / Amendment 4. A delegating Member may have only one proxy at a time, and a Member may act as proxy for only one Member at a time. / Amendment 5. While a delegation is in force, only the proxy may cast the delegating Member’s vote. The proxy may cast the delegating Member’s vote differently from his or her own vote and may cast either vote without casting the other. Voting by proxy shall apply to all forms of voting in plenary, including secret ballots. Both the name of the delegating Member and the name of the proxy shall be recorded in the minutes of the sitting and, for roll-call votes, the published voting results shall clearly indicate votes cast by proxy. / Amendment 6. A vote validly cast by proxy shall be attributed to the delegating Member and shall have the same effect as a vote cast in person by that Member. The validity of a vote cast by proxy and the voting result shall not be affected by any disagreement between the delegating Member and the proxy. A correction to a vote cast by proxy may be made only by the delegating Member, under the same conditions and in the same manner as for a vote cast in person, and shall not affect the validity of the vote or the voting result. / Amendment 7. The delegating Member may submit a written explanation of a vote cast on her behalf under the same conditions that would apply had she cast it in person, but may not give an oral explanation. The proxy may not submit or give an explanation of vote on behalf of the delegating Member. / Amendment 8. The Bureau shall lay down the practical arrangements necessary for the implementation of this Rule, including the forms to be used for the delegation and the applicable deadlines for the submission of those forms, as well as the list of supporting documents to be submitted. Those arrangements shall neither restrict nor extend the rights laid down in this Rule, nor modify the conditions laid down in this Rule. Those arrangements shall ensure the secrecy of secret ballots and the transparency, accountability, traceability, legal certainty and integrity of voting by proxy.
